note: Hebrew se'irim, literally "hairy ones / he-goats", here goat-shaped wilderness spirits worshipped in the open field; "devils" loses the specific goat imagery (cf. the goats of ch. 16).

kjv: the strangers which sojourn among you (Israel)
mine: the foreigners who reside among them (Israel)
note: The Masoretic text has betokham "among them" (also vv. 10, 13); the KJV's "among you" matches the Septuagint (en hymin) or harmonises with v. 12.

kjv: the blood [that] maketh an atonement for the soul
mine: the blood that makes atonement by means of the life
note: Hebrew bannephesh yekhapper, with the preposition be- most naturally instrumental ("by means of the life" contained in the blood) rather than "for the soul"; the KJV reading duplicates the preceding clause, while the instrumental sense explains why blood atones. Context: by means of the life (medium confidence). The verse grounds atonement in the fact that 'the life of the flesh is in the blood'; be- is most naturally instrumental, 'by means of the life' (ESV, NASB, NET), and avoids merely repeating 'for your lives'. A beth of price ('in exchange for life') is also seriously argued. Other possible meanings: (1) 'in exchange for the life' (life for life) — LXX anti psyches, several commentators; (2) 'as life' (the blood, being life, atones) — NRSV, NJPS; (3) 'for the soul/life' — Vulgate pro animae, KJV, NIV.
